A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALMI framework and ALMI-X dataset. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original simulation comparisons, curriculum and training ablations, foundation-model evaluations, dataset analyses, and real-robot demonstrations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds G1 simulation comparisons and experiments evaluating alternative adversarial training schemes.

M1.justification: The alternating upper/lower-body policies, command-space adversaries, curricula, PPO objectives, and foundation-model architecture remain unchanged. The additional training schemes in v3 Appendix E are experimental comparators.

E1.justification: V3 adds simulation evaluation on Unitree G1 using reference-motion velocity commands. The H1-2 tasks, CMU/AMASS motion coverage, ALMI-X dataset, and real-world demonstrations are retained.

E2.justification: V3 substantially broadens the evaluated alternatives: Table 5 adds ExBody2 and OmniH2O on G1, while Appendix E adds explicitly trained adversaries and jointly trained policies with adversarial rewards. Exbody and ALMI (whole) remain in the original H1-2 comparison.

E3.justification: The new G1 comparison supplies reference-motion velocities to ALMI, uses direct motion imitation for the baselines, and excludes terrain disturbances and pushes. Appendix E introduces action-clipping and adversarial-reward-weight sweeps. Existing H1-2 difficulty settings and foundation-model testing procedures are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix E directly tests the rationale for replacing learned adversaries with curriculum-based command sampling. Tables 14–15 examine adversary strength and simultaneous adversarial objectives, adding evidence about training failure and robustness beyond the retained iteration and arm-curriculum ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions per foundation-model command and retain point-estimate reporting. V3 adds no seed counts, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests; its affirmative statistical-significance checklist answer supplies no corresponding new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial comparative findings. Table 5 reports G1 survival of 0.9484 for ALMI, 0.3882 for OmniH2O, and 0.8848 for ExBody2; Table 14 reports zero survival for both tested explicit-adversary clipping scales. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v2. The retained H1-2, original ablation, and foundation-model tables match numerically.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, Assumption A.1, the Appendix A convergence proof, and the curriculum and optimization formulas are retained. Local policy/action-symbol corrections do not introduce different mathematical reasoning or results.

C1.justification: The principal ALMI, ALMI-X, and preliminary foundation-model contributions remain. V3 removes the abstract and introduction claims that collected trajectories are deployable on real robots, and the conclusion explicitly qualifies performance on highly dynamic tasks and the maturity of the foundation model.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit limitations concerning dancing and foundation-model data efficiency. Appendix E expands the interpretation of adversary-strength sensitivity and the practical justification for command-space sampling; Section 6.1 adds a cross-platform generalization interpretation of the G1 results.

D1.justification: V3 newly reports approximately 17 hours for the three training iterations and selection of converged baseline checkpoints. Its checklist supplies explicit code, foundation-model checkpoint, and dataset links, while Appendix C replaces the direct dataset link with the project page. These are documented access changes; availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V3 adds HOMIE, MORE, KungfuBot, KungfuBot2, and HumanoidGen/HGen-Bench to its research context. The overall positioning remains similar. Numerous other bibliography changes update publication metadata for works already cited in v2.

P1.justification: V3 makes local language and terminology corrections, adds Chi Zhang and the NeurIPS conference header, and inserts a conference checklist and two additional appendices. The existing main-text narrative and section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 5, 14, and 15, moves the existing reward tables from Appendix B into the main text as Tables 1–2, refreshes Figure 7, and adjusts table emphasis and captions. Existing figures and tables otherwise retain their content with layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The G1 comparisons and Appendix E experiments strengthen empirical support for the existing method, while narrower deployability claims and explicit limitations improve calibration. Added technical and access information also helps reproducibility. These benefits outweigh the new checklist's unsupported statistical-significance answer and stale cross-references, yielding a limited overall improvement.
